title: Most Foreign Workers Want to Stay in Japan
paragraphs: Japan needs more workers from other countries. So, do foreign workers want to stay in Japan for a long time? A new survey says that most of them do, but fewer than before.

The survey was done by Mynavi Global, a job-hunting service in Tokyo. Every year, it asks foreign people living in Japan about work. This year, 1,732 people answered the survey in January and February. The results were shared in July.

The survey found that 61.6% of the people want to work in Japan for more than five years. This is still more than half. But it is 14.7 points lower than last year. Also, 34.2% said they want to stay for two to five years, and 12.7% said they want to go back to their home country within one year.

Why do fewer people want to stay for a long time? The biggest reason is the weak yen. When the yen is weak, money earned in Japan is worth less in other countries. This is a problem for people who send money home to their families. Also, prices in Japan are going up, but salaries are not rising as fast.

Most of the people who answered the survey were from Southeast Asia. The largest group was from Vietnam, followed by Myanmar, Nepal, Indonesia and China. Many of them were students or people working in jobs such as nursing care, cleaning, building, factories and restaurants.
Even so, Japan is still a popular place to work for many people from other countries. The survey shows that most foreign workers still hope to build their lives and careers in Japan.
